lba_qa.q: A person saves Rs 100 in the first month and increases the savings by Rs 50 every month. How much will he save in the 12th month?
lba_qa.a:
This is an AP with first term a = 100 and common difference d = 50.
The nth term: a_n = a + (n - 1)d.
For the 12th month: a_12 = 100 + (12 - 1)(50) = 100 + 11 x 50 = 100 + 550 = 650.
So he will save Rs 650 in the 12th month.

lba_qa.q: A theatre has 20 seats in the first row, 22 in the second, 24 in the third, and so on. How many seats are there in the 15th row?
lba_qa.a:
This is an AP with a = 20, d = 2.
nth term: a_n = a + (n - 1)d.
a_15 = 20 + (15 - 1)(2) = 20 + 14 x 2 = 20 + 28 = 48.
So there are 48 seats in the 15th row.

lba_qa.q: A man takes a loan and repays it in monthly instalments. He pays Rs 1000 in the first month and increases each instalment by Rs 100. Find the total amount paid in the first 10 months.
lba_qa.a:
This is an AP with a = 1000, d = 100, n = 10.
Sum of n terms: S_n = (n/2)[2a + (n - 1)d].
S_10 = (10/2)[2(1000) + (10 - 1)(100)] = 5[2000 + 900] = 5 x 2900 = 14500.
So the total amount paid in 10 months is Rs 14,500.
lba_qa.topic: Sum of n terms of an AP (real-life)

lba_qa.q: Find the sum of the first 50 natural numbers (1 + 2 + 3 + ... + 50) using the AP formula.
lba_qa.a:
The natural numbers form an AP with a = 1, d = 1, n = 50.
Sum: S_n = (n/2)(first term + last term) = (n/2)(a + a_n).
Last term a_50 = 50.
S_50 = (50/2)(1 + 50) = 25 x 51 = 1275.
So the sum of the first 50 natural numbers is 1275.
lba_qa.topic: Sum of n terms of an AP

lba_qa.q: Which term of the AP 3, 8, 13, 18, ... is 78?
lba_qa.a:
Here a = 3, d = 8 - 3 = 5. Let the nth term be 78.
a_n = a + (n - 1)d = 78.
3 + (n - 1)(5) = 78, so (n - 1)(5) = 75, giving n - 1 = 15, so n = 16.
So 78 is the 16th term of the AP.

lba_qa.q: A salary starts at Rs 20000 with an annual increment of Rs 1500. What will the salary be in the 8th year?
lba_qa.a:
This is an AP with a = 20000, d = 1500.
nth term: a_n = a + (n - 1)d.
a_8 = 20000 + (8 - 1)(1500) = 20000 + 7 x 1500 = 20000 + 10500 = 30500.
So the salary in the 8th year will be Rs 30,500.

lba_qa.q: How can you check whether the sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, ... is an AP? Explain.
lba_qa.a:
A sequence is an AP if the difference between consecutive terms is always the same (constant common difference).
Here: 5 - 2 = 3; 8 - 5 = 3; 11 - 8 = 3.
Since the difference is the same (3) each time, the sequence is an AP with common difference d = 3.

lba_qa.q: The sum of the first n terms of an AP is given by S_n = 3n^2 + 2n. Find the first term and the common difference.
lba_qa.a:
First term a = S_1 = 3(1)^2 + 2(1) = 3 + 2 = 5.
S_2 = 3(2)^2 + 2(2) = 12 + 4 = 16.
Second term = S_2 - S_1 = 16 - 5 = 11.
Common difference d = second term - first term = 11 - 5 = 6.
So the first term is 5 and the common difference is 6.
lba_qa.topic: Sum of n terms of an AP

lba_qa.q: A farmer plants trees in rows: 1 tree in the first row, 2 in the second, 3 in the third, and so on up to 20 rows. How many trees in total?
lba_qa.a:
This forms an AP: 1, 2, 3, ..., 20 with a = 1, d = 1, n = 20.
Sum = (n/2)(first + last) = (20/2)(1 + 20) = 10 x 21 = 210.
So the farmer plants 210 trees in total.
lba_qa.topic: Sum of n terms of an AP (real-life)
